proposed.sourceName: American Halal Foundation (AHF) — 'Are Mono Diglycerides Halal?' (Azmi Anees)
proposed.paraphrase: AHF classifies E471 (mono- and diglycerides) as source-dependent: halal only when derived from 100% plant oils (palm, soy, canola) or carrying a recognized halal logo; non-zabiha beef and pork-derived forms are not halal. Because labels rarely disclose the source, most certifiers including AHF advise consumers to AVOID E471 unless it is explicitly labeled 'vegetable mono & diglycerides' or the finished product bears a halal mark — i.e. it is doubtful (mushbooh) at the general position.

proposed.sourceName: Darul Iftaa, Jaamia Madinatul Uloom (Trinidad) — 'Is Mono and di-glycerides (E471) permissible?' (Mufti Arshad Ali)
proposed.paraphrase: The fatwa holds that E471 is permissible when plant-derived and impermissible when animal-derived unless the animal was slaughtered per Islamic law; it advises Muslims to avoid products containing mono- and diglycerides unless labeled 100% vegetable, and to contact the manufacturer to verify origin when the source is unlisted — treating undisclosed-origin E471 as doubtful.

researcherNote: E471 seeded general = grade 3 (Questionable — contested). Undisclosed source: majority commercial E471 is now plant (~60%) but animal (incl. pork/non-zabiha) remains common and labels don't disclose, so mainstream/general practice treats it as genuinely doubtful — matches grade 3. Two independent tier-1 sources (AHF certification body + Trinidad Darul Iftaa), both directly supporting the doubtful/verify-source stance. High-traffic -> two independent sources present. APPROVED by owner 2026-07-01.
